title: Fewshot Bridgework Anthology (scratch)
content:
Goal: collect compact few-shot scaffolds that are resilient to token drift and hallucination for common Redwood surface tasks (summarize, classify, extract, rephrase). This is a personal lab - lots of half-baked ideas, quick probes, and failure cases. Keep it short and iteratively prune later.

Top-level notes / heuristics observed so far:
- System + one-line role hint => often more stable for formatting, but less creative for paraphrase tasks.
- Add a predicate example (positive and negative) rather than many neutrals when disambiguating edge cases.
- 3-shot with contrast (good vs bad) reduces hallucinatory insertions for extraction tasks.
- Temperature sweeps matter: 0.0-0.2 for strict extractions, 0.3-0.6 for phrasing. Watch token budget.
- Prompt-framing: "You are a concise transformer that only outputs JSON" style prompts help, but model still emits commentary occasionally; add a final explicit: "OUTPUT ONLY JSON or EXACT MATCH WILL BE CONSIDERED INVALID."

Experiment set A: compact extractors (invoice fields)
Objective: pull invoice_number, total_cents, vendor_normalized
Design constraints: keep examples < 120 tokens, show failure mode where vendor uses parentheses, dashes, weird casing.
Shotset 1 (baseline): system: "Extract fields exactly as JSON keys: invoice_number, total_cents, vendor"
1) Text: "Invoice # 2023-332 - ACME, Inc. Total: $1,234.56" -> {invoice_number: "2023-332", total_cents: 123456, vendor: "ACME, Inc."}
2) Text: "Inv:20230001 | Acme LLC (HQ) | Amount due 99.00 USD" -> {invoice_number: "20230001", total_cents: 9900, vendor: "Acme LLC (HQ)"}
3) Text: "Receipt 42 — acme.co.uk — total EUR 12" -> {invoice_number: "42", total_cents: 1200, vendor: "acme.co.uk"}

Notes: baseline often strips parentheses from vendor when vendor_normalized required; add explicit normalization examples.

Shotset 2 (contrastive): include a bad example to show what NOT to extract
Good example: see above 1
Bad example: "Order 2023-332 (customer ref: 7) - payment $1,234.56" -> EXTRACT invoice_number: "2023-332" BUT vendor: "" (empty) because no vendor present; model sometimes invents vendor name "Unknown". Show negative example mapping vendor to null.

Failure cases observed:
- Model infers currency conversions unless currency is explicit. (Adds comments like "~USD")
- If invoice has multiple numbers, tends to pick first number that _looks_ like invoice; need predicate like "prefer patterns with 4+ digits + dash".

TODO: create small set of regex-derived checks to post-validate. If postcheck fails, return nulls and a short error_code.

Experiment set B: conversational instruction paraphrasing
Objective: produce a 1-line rewrite that conserves intent and removes directive verbs (so it's polite microcopy).
Shotset (2-shot) examples:
1) Input: "Remind the user to verify identity before checkout" -> Output: "Please verify your identity to finish checkout."
2) Input: "Force a password reset if suspicious activity detected" -> Output: "We recommend resetting your password for safety."

Probes: when temperature >0.5, model adds extra explanation. For UI microcopy we want concise. Hard constrain: max 10 tokens. Model often violates, so use a token-aware cutoff in system message.

Edge failure: model flips polarity when input is already polite (adds hedging like "you might want to consider"). Solution attempt: include an explicit positive and negative example where negative = "do not soften polarity".

Experiment set C: fewshot classification with oddballs (intent taxonomy)
Taxonomy: support_billing, support_technical, sales_inquiry, feedback
Shotset 4-shot with one oddball negative example to teach "unknown" mapping
Examples:
- "I can't log in to the dashboard" -> support_technical
- "How do I add seats to my plan?" -> sales_inquiry
- "Your API charged me twice" -> support_billing
- "Love the new UI" -> feedback
Oddball: "What is the weather in Boston?" -> unknown

Notes: Model often maps oddballs to nearest label; adding explicit 'unknown' examples helps but reduces precision on ambiguous natural language. Tradeoff. Consider thresholding on prediction confidence (logprob) when available.

Meta-failures and debugging snippets (raw outputs copied during runs):
- Extraction probe (shotset 1) returned vendor: "Acme LLC HQ" instead of "Acme LLC (HQ)" -> parentheses removed.
- Classification probe labeled "chargeback" as sales_inquiry (wrong) when text contained both billing + sales phrasing.

Ideas to try next:
- Use a tiny context window for prefix-only examples (avoid long conversational preamble).
- Add a "surgical fewshot" template: 1 neutral system line, 2 positive canonical examples, 1 explicit negative (contrasting) example, then a 1-line instruction, then the target. Seems to work best for extractions.
- Token-budget-aware fallback: if incoming prompt > X tokens, switch to a 1-shot strict extractor that returns only keys it can find reliably.

Quick rough templates (copyable):
TEMPLATE: SURGICAL-EXTRACTOR
SYSTEM: "You are a strict extractor. Output only valid JSON mapping: invoice_number, total_cents, vendor. If a field is not present, output null. Do not add commentary."
EXAMPLES: 2 good + 1 bad (see Shotset 2)
INSTRUCTION (1 line): "Extract fields now from the following text:"
INPUT: "<raw text>"

TEMPLATE: POLITE-REWRITE
SYSTEM: "You are a UX copy assistant. Rewrite input into a single courteous sentence, max 12 tokens, preserve intent exactly."
EXAMPLES: 2 examples (see Experiment B)
INPUT: "<raw microcopy>"

Small evaluation plan (manual for now):
- Create 200 random samples per task from historical logs (anonymized).
- Run each template with temperature 0.0, 0.3, 0.6 and record exact-match and relaxed F1 for extraction; top-1 accuracy and unknown-recall for classification; token-length distribution for rewrites.
- Surface top 10 failure cases weekly in PR review.

Open questions (unresolved):
- How to canonicalize vendor names robustly inside prompt without blowing token budget? (Would a short inline normalization table for 20 known vendors reduce errors?)
- When to prefer negative examples vs more positive ones? heuristics?
- Is it worth instrumenting a lightweight probe lambda that quickly re-queries with stricter system message on low-confidence responses? (Good for Dedicated customers with latency budgets?)

Random notes to self (todo fragments):
- Add a tiny python harness to turn these shotsets into JSONL for eval.
- Try 4-bit quantized local runs to sanity-check before wide hosted experiments.
- Share with Riley for UX microcopy set.

Appendix: hand-curated odd examples to include in training/eval sets (copy into dataset):
1) "Order #7: Payment via ACH - no vendor listed" -> extraction should yield invoice_number=7 vendor=null
2) "Invoice: 00001234 / Vendor: — / Amount 0.00" -> vendor = null (em dash indicates missing)
3) "Reference: 2023-332 (ACME PO 77) - TOTAL USD 1234.56" -> invoice_number prefer 2023-332, ignore PO
4) "Can you tell me when the promo ends?" -> classification -> unknown or feedback depending on context

End of scratchpad. Will prune/formalize to a single collection file next sprint.

-- a.p.
